The shortest is the triangle A, B, C, drawn in the accent color, so the girth is 3." width="100%"} The girth is the length of the shortest cycle in the graph. Returns `None` if the graph is acyclic (a forest/tree, or a DAG). In a directed graph, cycles follow the edge directions. Uses BFS from each node to detect shortest cycles efficiently. The implementation includes fast-path checks: - returns `1` for graphs with self-loops - returns `2` for undirected graphs with multi-edges, or directed graphs with a pair of opposite edges - returns `3` or more for cycles found via BFS ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Length of shortest cycle, or `None` if acyclic. - 1: Graph contains a self-loop (edge from node to itself) - 2: Undirected graph contains multi-edges (duplicate edges), or directed graph contains edges both ways between two nodes - 3+: Shortest cycle length found via BFS - `None`: Graph is acyclic (tree/forest) ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find girth of a cycle graph: ::: {#cf448749 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A")]) ) # Returns 4 (cycle length) graph.girth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: Self-loops have girth 1: ::: {#c0976909 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_node(label="A").add_edge("A", "A") # Returns 1 graph.girth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Triangles have girth 3: ::: {#e6156c03 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) # Returns 3 graph.girth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Trees have no cycles: ::: {#ed1678a3 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_balanced_tree(k=2, h=3) # Returns None (trees have no cycles) tree.girth() ``` :::
